record.paper_title: Geometric and Topological Obstructions to Various Immersions in Submanifold Theory and Some Related Open Problems
record.original_question: For a Riemannian manifold M, what topological, Riemannian, or other geometric conditions obstruct the existence of a slant immersion of M into complex Euclidean m-space C^m? A slant submanifold is one for which, for every nonzero tangent vector X, the Wirtinger angle between JX and the tangent space is constant, independent of both the point of M and the choice of X.

evidence.quote: A submanifold M of M~ is called a slant submanifold if the Wirtinger angle theta(X) is constant; so it is independent of the choice of p in M and of X in T_pM.
Problem 4.1. What are the obstructions to slant immersions of a Riemannian manifold into a complex Euclidean m-space C^m?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}^m$ denote complex Euclidean $m$-space equipped with its standard Hermitian structure, with almost complex structure $J$ and standard flat Kähler metric. For an isometric immersion $f:M\to\mathbb{C}^m$ of a Riemannian manifold $M$, and for a point $p\in M$ and a nonzero tangent vector $X\in T_pM$, the Wirtinger angle $\theta(X)\in[0,\pi/2]$ is defined as the angle between $JX$ (viewed via $df$) and the tangent space $df(T_pM)\subset T_{f(p)}\mathbb{C}^m$. The immersion $f$ is called a slant immersion if $\theta(X)$ is constant, i.e.\ independent of both $p\in M$ and of the nonzero vector $X\in T_pM$. (Holomorphic immersions correspond to $\theta\equiv 0$ and totally real (in particular Lagrangian) immersions to $\theta\equiv\pi/2$; proper slant means $0<\theta<\pi/2$.)

Determine necessary topological, Riemannian, or other geometric conditions on $M$ that obstruct the existence of a slant isometric immersion $f:M\to\mathbb{C}^m$ for some $m$, and in particular characterize which Riemannian manifolds admit a proper slant immersion into some complex Euclidean space.
artifact.status_search_result: A general characterization of obstructions to slant immersions of arbitrary Riemannian manifolds into complex Euclidean space does not appear in the literature. Partial results exist for special classes (e.g., warped products, Lagrangian/totally real cases, and slant submanifolds in complex space forms), but no comprehensive answer is documented, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: New Obstructions to Warped Product Immersions in Complex Space Forms
status_evidence.snippet: obstructions to the minimality of warped product pointwise semi-slant submanifolds in a complex space form
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to develop partial obstructions for slant-type immersions, indicating the general question remains active.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Submanifolds: A Survey (Chen)
status_evidence.snippet: survey of Riemannian submanifolds including slant submanifolds
status_evidence.claim: Survey treats slant submanifolds without providing a complete list of obstructions to slant immersions into complex Euclidean space.
